title: Mexico — LFPDPPP
subtitle: Discovering and masking Mexican personal data: direct identifiers with valid check digits, quasi-identifiers, the sensitive data of article 2 and the financial and patrimonial data of article 7.

sections.title: About this profile set
body: This profile set finds the personal data in a Mexican database and masks it, so that a non-production copy — for testing, development, training or analytics — no longer identifies anyone.
Masking only names and CURPs does not achieve that: a birth date, a sex and a small municipality single people out on their own. The set works in the same layers the risk does:

list: **Direct identifiers** — CURP, RFC, NSS, INE voter key, names, contact details, CLABE and cards, documents, devices, vehicles, free text.
**Quasi-identifiers** — birth date, age, sex, municipality, locality, colonia, postal code, occupation, employer, schooling.
**Sensitive data** — ethnic origin and indigenous language, health, genetic information, religious, philosophical and moral beliefs, political opinions, sexual preference, and union membership.
**Financial and patrimonial data** — credit bureau records, debts, income, assets, retirement savings, housing credit, social security, social programs, socioeconomic level, tax regime.
**Criminal records** — records and case numbers.

body: Everything the set needs travels with it: loading it creates its domains, classifiers, algorithms and lookup files, and sending it to a Masking Engine sends all of them.

sections.title: The LFPDPPP in brief
body: The Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares was published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación on 20 March 2025 and took effect the next day, repealing the law of 2010. Its last amendment (14 November 2025) touched only its supplementary procedural rules. The INAI was dissolved: the authority is now the **Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno**. The public sector has its own law, the Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados, issued the same day.
What matters for a copy of production data:

list: **Personal data** is any information about an identified or identifiable person — identifiable directly or indirectly, through any information (art. 2, V).

**Sensitive data** are those that touch the most intimate sphere of a person or whose misuse may lead to discrimination or serious risk. The law names, as examples and not as a closed list, data that may reveal racial or ethnic origin, present or future health, genetic information, religious, philosophical and moral beliefs, political opinions and sexual preference (art. 2, VI). They need express written consent, and databases of sensitive data may only be created for legitimate, specific purposes (art. 8).
**Financial and patrimonial data** need express consent (art. 7).

**Purpose.** Data may only be processed for the purposes of the privacy notice; a different purpose needs new consent (art. 11). Development and testing are rarely among the purposes a customer agreed to.

**Dissociation** — a procedure after which data can no longer be associated with the person nor, by their structure, content or level of detail, identify them (art. 2, IX). Consent is not required for data subjected to prior dissociation (art. 9, III).

**Security.** Administrative, technical and physical measures proportional to the sensitivity of the data (art. 18); breaches that significantly affect people must be reported to them (art. 19); everyone involved keeps confidentiality (art. 20).

**Sanctions.** Fines up to 320,000 times the UMA, which may be doubled for sensitive data (art. 59); prison of three months to five years for the crimes of chapter XII, doubled for sensitive data (arts. 62 to 64).

body: A test environment filled with production data is processing for a purpose the privacy notice does not cover, and holds sensitive and financial data outside the controls built for them. A dissociated copy is the route the law itself provides: that is what this set is for.

Two notes on the categories. The 2010 law listed **union membership** as sensitive; the 2025 text no longer names it. Its list is not exhaustive and union membership still exposes people to discrimination, so the set keeps it. **Biometric data** are not named either; they identify a person by definition and are treated as sensitive here.

body.note: This document describes technical controls. Whether a copy counts as dissociated is a legal assessment of the whole environment — its access, its retention, what else is joined to it — and not of the profile set alone.

sections.title: Using the set

list: **Load** — *Settings → Profile Sets → Load*. Loading again resets every object of the set to how it ships.
**Send to Delphix** — from the profile set, or with *Send everything to Delphix*. Domains, algorithms and files go first.
**Profile** — run a profiling job with the set, then review the domains it assigned before masking.
**Mask** — run the masking job. Use the same engine key in every environment to keep masked values consistent across systems.

body: The assignment threshold is 60%. An unambiguous column name reaches it alone; an ambiguous one — `NOMBRE`, `RESULTADO`, `CIUDAD` — needs the values to agree. A column with a meaningless name (`CAMPO1`, `OBS`) is still found when its values have a recognizable shape or vocabulary: a CURP, an RFC, an INE voter key, a CLABE, a plate, a municipality.

Column names are recognized in Spanish, in the abbreviations of Mexican systems (`AP_PATERNO`, `FEC_NAC`, `NUM_EXT`, `CVE_MUN`, `SDI`), in the attribute names of CFDI 4.0 invoices (`RfcReceptor`, `DomicilioFiscalReceptor`, `RegimenFiscalReceptor`) and in English.

body.tip: Before masking, inventory the binary columns (BLOB, images, PDF). Onboarding processes often store photos of the INE credential: the CURP and the voter key stay readable in the image. Report those columns as residual risk.

groups.title: Direct identifiers
intro: Data that identify a person on their own. The national keys — CURP, RFC, NSS, CLABE — keep a valid check digit after masking, because applications validate them and a test environment where they fail validation tests nothing.

groups.title: Quasi-identifiers
intro: Data that identify no one alone but do in combination. Mexico has 2,469 municipalities, and 1,505 of them had fewer than 20,000 inhabitants in 2020: a birth date, a sex and one of those municipalities point to a handful of people. These attributes are generalized or shifted rather than replaced, so the data keep their analytical value.

groups.title: Sensitive data
intro: The categories of article 2, section VI — ethnic origin, health, genetic information, beliefs, political opinions, sexual preference — together with gender identity, sexual life, biometrics and union membership. A categorical value is replaced by another of the same category, so the column keeps a realistic content; where the values share no vocabulary, they are suppressed.

groups.title: Financial and patrimonial data
intro: Article 7 requires express consent for financial and patrimonial data — a regime of its own, between ordinary and sensitive data, that GDPR-based templates do not have. It covers more than bank accounts: a credit bureau record, a daily wage, a housing credit, a social program or a tax regime tell as much about a person's economic situation as an income. Categories are replaced within their own notation; amounts are mapped into a plausible range with no link to the real value.

groups.title: Criminal records
intro: Not named by the LFPDPPP, but among the data most likely to lead to discrimination, which is what article 2 describes as sensitive. They are handled with the same care.

MX_L1_CURP.title: CURP
MX_L1_CURP.what: The Clave Única de Registro de Población: 18 characters built from the names (4 letters), the birth date, the sex, the state of birth, three internal consonants, a differentiator — a digit for people born before 2000, a letter after — and a check digit. `HEGA850720MDFRRL04`. The key of almost every Mexican record, and a quasi-identifier in itself: it carries the birth date, sex and state.
MX_L1_CURP.masking: Letters become other letters (vowel for vowel, consonant for consonant), the birth date another valid date of the same decade, the sex and state other values, the consonants and differentiator other ones of their kind — and the check digit is recomputed, so every masked CURP passes validation. The mapping is one-to-one: a CURP used as a key cannot collide. See *Check digits computed by the set*.

MX_L1_RFC.title: RFC
MX_L1_RFC.what: The Registro Federal de Contribuyentes: 13 characters for a person (4 letters, birth date, 2-character differentiator, check digit), 12 for a company. `HEGA850720ABA`. Appears in payroll, supplier and CFDI invoice tables.
MX_L1_RFC.masking: Same treatment as the CURP, with the SAT's modulo 11 check digit, `A` included. A person's RFC shares its first ten characters with their CURP, and both are masked with the same algorithms: after masking they still share them. Company RFCs are masked too — a column mixes both, and the incorporation date of a small company can point to its owner. An RFC without differentiator (10 characters) keeps its shape.

MX_L1_NSS.title: Social security number (NSS)
MX_L1_NSS.what: The IMSS number: 11 digits holding the subdelegation, registration year, birth year, a sequence and a check digit. Present in every payroll and HR system.
MX_L1_NSS.masking: Replaced by another NSS that passes the same Luhn check — the check of payment cards, which the Payment Card framework keeps valid. The mapping is one-to-one. Written with dashes, it is masked digit by digit, without a valid check digit.

MX_L1_CLAVE_ELECTOR.title: INE voter key
MX_L1_CLAVE_ELECTOR.what: The clave de elector of the INE credential: 6 consonants from the names, birth date, state number, sex and a 3-digit differentiator. `GRHRAL85072009M100`. The INE credential is the most used identity document in Mexico.
MX_L1_CLAVE_ELECTOR.masking: Consonants mapped, birth date through the same algorithm as in the CURP (so a person's CURP and voter key keep the same masked date), state and sex replaced, differentiator mapped. The key has no check digit.

MX_L1_CREDENCIAL_INE.title: INE credential numbers
MX_L1_CREDENCIAL_INE.what: The numbers that identify the physical credential: OCR (13 digits), CIC (9 digits), the citizen identifier and the issue number.
MX_L1_CREDENCIAL_INE.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_NOMBRE.title: Given names
MX_L1_NOMBRE.what: First and middle names (`NOMBRES`, `PRIMER_NOMBRE`), including compound names such as `María Guadalupe` or `José Luis`.
MX_L1_NOMBRE.masking: Each word is replaced by a Mexican given name from a list of 255, keeping the number of words and the case. More than three words are masked character by character.

MX_L1_APELLIDO.title: Surnames
MX_L1_APELLIDO.what: Paternal and maternal surnames, in one column or two.
MX_L1_APELLIDO.masking: Each word is replaced by one of the 337 most frequent Mexican surnames, keeping the number of words and the case.

MX_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.title: Full name
MX_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.what: Given names and both surnames in one column, in Mexican order, or as `SURNAMES, NAMES`. Also the name of a titular, beneficiary, insured person or invoice receiver.
MX_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.masking: Given names become given names and surnames become surnames, by position: one word is a name, two are name and surname, three are name and two surnames, four are two names and two surnames. A comma separates surnames from names.

MX_L1_EMAIL.title: E-mail
MX_L1_EMAIL.masking: The name and domain are mapped character by character and the top-level domain becomes `.test`, reserved for tests: a masked address can never receive mail.

MX_L1_TELEFONO.title: Phone number
MX_L1_TELEFONO.what: Landlines and mobiles. Since August 2019 every Mexican number has 10 digits: a 2-digit area code for Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey (55, 56, 33, 81), 3 digits elsewhere.
MX_L1_TELEFONO.masking: The subscriber digits are masked; `+52`, the old mobile `1`, the area code and the separators stay. A number that does not have the shape of a Mexican number is masked digit by digit.

MX_L1_DIRECCION.title: Address
MX_L1_DIRECCION.what: The street line of an address: street, exterior and interior number, or block and lot (`Mz. 12 Lt. 5`).
MX_L1_DIRECCION.masking: Replaced by one of 3,000 fictitious Mexican addresses on common street names, with interior numbers and blocks and lots in realistic proportions.

MX_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.title: Address details
MX_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.what: Exterior and interior numbers, block, lot, building or tower kept in their own columns.
MX_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_CLABE.title: CLABE
MX_L1_CLABE.what: The 18-digit standardized bank key: bank (3), plaza (3), account (11) and check digit. Used in every SPEI transfer and payroll deposit.
MX_L1_CLABE.masking: The bank code stays, so reports by bank still add up; plaza and account are masked and the check digit (weights 3, 7, 1, modulo 10) recomputed. Every masked CLABE is valid and the mapping is one-to-one.

MX_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.title: Bank account
MX_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.what: Account numbers other than the CLABE: checking, savings, payroll.
MX_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_TARJETA.title: Payment card
MX_L1_TARJETA.masking: Replaced by another card number that still passes the Luhn check. Values that do not look like a card pass unchanged instead of failing the row.

MX_L1_PASAPORTE.title: Passport
MX_L1_PASAPORTE.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.title: Immigration document
MX_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.what: Temporary and permanent resident cards, immigration forms, visas and foreign identity numbers.
MX_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_CEDULA_PROFESIONAL.title: Professional license
MX_L1_CEDULA_PROFESIONAL.what: The number of the cédula profesional issued by the SEP. The registry is public: the number leads straight to the person's name.

MX_L1_LICENCIA_CONDUCIR.title: Driver's license
MX_L1_LICENCIA_CONDUCIR.what: State and federal driver's license numbers.
MX_L1_LICENCIA_CONDUCIR.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_EFIRMA.title: e.firma certificate
MX_L1_EFIRMA.what: The 20-digit serial number of an e.firma (FIEL) or digital seal certificate issued by the SAT.

MX_L1_IP.title: IP address
MX_L1_IP.what: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of users and devices.
MX_L1_IP.masking: Each IPv4 octet is mapped to a number from 1 to 254; an IPv6 address is mapped as hexadecimal.

MX_L1_DISPOSITIVO.title: Device identifier
MX_L1_DISPOSITIVO.what: IMEI, MAC address, advertising and session identifiers, device serial numbers.
MX_L1_DISPOSITIVO.masking: Hexadecimal stays hexadecimal and digits stay digits, so the value keeps its format.

MX_L1_PLACA.title: License plate
MX_L1_PLACA.what: Vehicle plates in the formats of NOM-001-SCT-2-2016 (`URU-197-A`), Mexico City (`A-12-BCD`) and older series.
MX_L1_PLACA.masking: Letters map among the letters plates use — never `I`, `O` or `Q` — and digits among digits: the masked plate is still a valid plate. The state series is not preserved.

MX_L1_NIV.title: Vehicle identification number
MX_L1_NIV.what: The NIV (VIN), engine and chassis numbers and the REPUVE registration.
MX_L1_NIV.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format. The check digit of North American VINs is not recomputed.

MX_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.title: Contract and customer numbers
MX_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.what: Contract, policy, credit, customer, member, employee and payroll numbers — internal keys that lead to a person in the source system.
MX_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format, so the same number masks the same way in every table.

MX_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.title: Username and social media
MX_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.what: Usernames, logins, aliases and social media handles.
MX_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L1_CREDENCIAL.title: Credentials
MX_L1_CREDENCIAL.what: Passwords and their hashes, PINs, tokens, API keys, the SAT CIEC password and security questions.
MX_L1_CREDENCIAL.masking: Every character becomes `X`. A credential has no place in a test environment.

MX_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.title: Geolocation
MX_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.what: Latitude and longitude of homes, deliveries or devices.
MX_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.masking: The integer part and first decimal stay — about 11 km — and the rest is masked: the place is generalized, not moved to another region.

MX_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.title: Free text
MX_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.what: Observations, comments, complaints, address references and notes where people write identifiers in the middle of a sentence.
MX_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.masking: CURPs, RFCs, INE voter keys, e-mails, 10-digit phones, NSS, card and CLABE numbers, plates and IPs are replaced by `[DATO]`; given names and surnames from the lists by `[NOMBRE]`.

MX_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.title: Birth date
MX_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.what: The strongest quasi-identifier: with sex and municipality it singles out most people.
MX_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.masking: Shifted up to 60 days, the same way in every table for the same date.

MX_L2_ANIO_NACIMIENTO.title: Birth year
MX_L2_ANIO_NACIMIENTO.what: The year of birth stored on its own.
MX_L2_ANIO_NACIMIENTO.masking: The decade stays and the last digit is masked — with the same mapping as the year inside a CURP, RFC or voter key.

MX_L2_EDAD.title: Age
MX_L2_EDAD.masking: The decade stays and the unit is masked (37 → 3x); 100 and over becomes 90, because very old ages are rare enough to identify.

MX_L2_FECHA_EVENTO.title: Life event dates
MX_L2_FECHA_EVENTO.what: Dates of death, marriage, hiring and dismissal, IMSS registration, disability leave, hospitalization, diagnosis, childbirth, arrest.

MX_L2_SEXO.title: Sex
MX_L2_SEXO.masking: Replaced within its own vocabulary. `H`/`M` uses the same lookup as the sex inside a CURP or voter key, so the three stay consistent.

MX_L2_MUNICIPIO.title: Municipality
MX_L2_MUNICIPIO.what: Municipality or Mexico City borough. 1,505 of the 2,469 municipalities had fewer than 20,000 inhabitants in the 2020 census.
MX_L2_MUNICIPIO.masking: A municipality under 20,000 inhabitants becomes the nearest municipality of the same state that has at least 20,000; larger ones stay. The result is a real, nearby municipality. Names without accents and in capitals are recognized. A name shared by several municipalities is generalized only when all of them are small.

MX_L2_CLAVE_MUNICIPIO.title: Municipality code
MX_L2_CLAVE_MUNICIPIO.what: The 5-digit INEGI geostatistical code of a municipality (state + municipality), with or without the leading zero.
MX_L2_CLAVE_MUNICIPIO.masking: Generalized exactly like the municipality name, without the ambiguity of homonyms.

MX_L2_LOCALIDAD.title: Locality
MX_L2_LOCALIDAD.what: Locality, town, ejido, rancho or community — often a few hundred inhabitants — and place of birth.
MX_L2_LOCALIDAD.masking: Replaced by the name of a municipality of over 100,000 inhabitants: still a place, no longer theirs.

MX_L2_COLONIA.title: Colonia
MX_L2_COLONIA.what: Colonia, fraccionamiento, barrio or housing unit: with the postal code, it narrows an address down to a few blocks.
MX_L2_COLONIA.masking: Replaced by a common colonia name (`Centro`, `Del Valle`, `Las Flores`).

MX_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.title: Postal code
MX_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.what: Five digits: the first two are the state or Mexico City borough. Also the fiscal address of CFDI invoices.
MX_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.masking: The first three digits stay and the last two become `00` (`06760` → `06700`).

MX_L2_NACIONALIDAD.title: Nationality
MX_L2_NACIONALIDAD.what: Nationality or country of birth. A foreign nationality is rare in most tables, and rarity identifies.
MX_L2_NACIONALIDAD.masking: Replaced by a nationality from a list of the most frequent in Mexico.

MX_L2_ESTADO_CIVIL.title: Marital status
MX_L2_ESTADO_CIVIL.what: Single, married, free union, separated, divorced, widowed.

MX_L2_OCUPACION.title: Occupation
MX_L2_OCUPACION.what: Occupation, profession or position. A rare position identifies on its own.
MX_L2_OCUPACION.masking: Replaced by one of 40 common occupations.

MX_L2_EMPLEADOR.title: Employer
MX_L2_EMPLEADOR.masking: Replaced by a fictitious Mexican company.

MX_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.title: Schooling
MX_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.what: Highest level of schooling, in INEGI's categories.
MX_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.masking: Replaced by another level of the same scale.

MX_L2_ESCUELA.title: School
MX_L2_ESCUELA.what: Name of a school, high school or university.
MX_L2_ESCUELA.masking: Replaced by a generic school name.

MX_L2_CCT.title: School code (CCT)
MX_L2_CCT.what: The Clave de Centro de Trabajo of a school: state, type, number and a letter (`09DPR1234X`).
MX_L2_CCT.masking: Character by character, keeping the format.

MX_L2_DEPENDIENTES.title: Dependents and children
MX_L2_DEPENDIENTES.what: Number of economic dependents, children or household members.
MX_L2_DEPENDIENTES.masking: Values up to 5 stay; larger ones become 5, because large households are rare.

MX_L3_ETNIA.title: Ethnic origin
MX_L3_ETNIA.what: Indigenous people, Afro-Mexican self-identification or ethnic group. Named first in the sensitive data of article 2.
MX_L3_ETNIA.masking: A yes/no flag stays a flag; a people becomes another from a list of the most numerous indigenous peoples and the Afro-Mexican people, including unlisted ones such as `Kumiai`.

MX_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.title: Indigenous language
MX_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.what: Whether a person speaks an indigenous language, and which. It reveals ethnic origin as surely as self-identification, and INEGI asks it in every census.
MX_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.masking: A flag stays a flag; a language becomes another from a list of the most spoken.

MX_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.title: Diagnosis
MX_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.what: Diagnoses, ICD-10 codes, conditions, allergies and pathological history.
MX_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.masking: An ICD-10 code becomes a common code in the same format (`F32.9` → `J45.9`), a description a common diagnosis. The mapping hides the sensitive conditions — HIV, mental health, addictions — among ordinary ones.

MX_L3_SALUD_MEDICAMENTO.title: Medication
MX_L3_SALUD_MEDICAMENTO.what: Prescribed medicines. An antiretroviral or an antipsychotic reveals the diagnosis.

MX_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.title: Health record identifiers
MX_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.what: Clinical file numbers (NOM-004-SSA3-2012), episode, prescription, bed and disability certificate numbers.
MX_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.title: Clinical notes
MX_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.what: Medical, progress, admission and discharge notes, current illness, physical examination — free text where names and CURPs appear.
MX_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.masking: The same free text redaction as other text: identifiers become `[DATO]`, names `[NOMBRE]`. The clinical content stays.

MX_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.title: Test results
MX_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.what: Laboratory and imaging results: HIV, viral load, glucose, HbA1c, pregnancy and drug tests.
MX_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

MX_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.title: Disability
MX_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.what: Type or degree of disability, in the categories of the 2020 census.
MX_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.masking: A flag stays a flag; a type becomes another census category.

MX_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.title: Sexual and reproductive health
MX_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.what: Pregnancy, gestational age, legal interruption of pregnancy, contraception, fertility, sexually transmitted infections.
MX_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.masking: A flag stays a flag and a number gets other digits; anything else becomes `Sin información`.

MX_L3_SALUD_MENTAL_ADICCIONES.title: Mental health and addictions
MX_L3_SALUD_MENTAL_ADICCIONES.what: Psychiatric and psychological care, disorders, suicide risk, substance use and treatment.
MX_L3_SALUD_MENTAL_ADICCIONES.masking: Suppressed to `Sin información`; flags and codes keep their shape.

MX_L3_BIOMETRICO.title: Biometric data
MX_L3_BIOMETRICO.what: Fingerprint and facial templates, iris, voice and digitized signatures stored as text.
MX_L3_BIOMETRICO.masking: Every character becomes `X`. Binary columns cannot be masked by the set; see *Limits*.

MX_L3_INFORMACION_GENETICA.title: Genetic information
MX_L3_INFORMACION_GENETICA.what: DNA profiles, genotypes, mutations, genetic screening and paternity tests — named by article 2.

MX_L3_PREFERENCIA_SEXUAL.title: Sexual preference
MX_L3_PREFERENCIA_SEXUAL.what: Sexual orientation — *preferencia sexual* in the words of the law.
MX_L3_PREFERENCIA_SEXUAL.masking: Replaced by another value of the same scale.

MX_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.title: Gender identity
MX_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.what: Self-perceived gender identity and legal gender recognition.
MX_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.masking: Replaced by another value of the same scale.

MX_L3_RELIGION.title: Religion
MX_L3_RELIGION.what: Religious affiliation — religious beliefs are named by article 2.
MX_L3_RELIGION.masking: Replaced by a religion group of the 2020 census, including unlisted churches such as `Luz del Mundo`.

MX_L3_CREENCIA_FILOSOFICA_MORAL.title: Philosophical and moral beliefs
MX_L3_CREENCIA_FILOSOFICA_MORAL.what: Convictions, conscientious objection, ethical positions — the article 2 wording for beliefs that are not religious.

MX_L3_OPINION_POLITICA.title: Political opinions
MX_L3_OPINION_POLITICA.what: Ideology, political position, voting intention and electoral preference.
MX_L3_OPINION_POLITICA.masking: Replaced by another position of the same scale.

MX_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.title: Party membership
MX_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.what: Party membership or sympathy. A party list reveals political opinion.
MX_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.masking: Replaced by one of the national parties registered in 2026, including those that lost registration (`PRD`).

MX_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.title: Union membership
MX_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.what: Union membership, union dues, section and unionized or trust worker status.
MX_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.masking: A flag stays a flag; anything else becomes `Sin información`.

MX_FIN_BURO_CREDITO.title: Credit bureau record
MX_FIN_BURO_CREDITO.what: Buró de Crédito and Círculo de Crédito data: payment behaviour codes (MOP), score, arrears status, write-offs.
MX_FIN_BURO_CREDITO.masking: A MOP code becomes another MOP code, a 3-digit score other digits, a status another status.

MX_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.title: Debt amount
MX_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.what: Outstanding balance, amount owed, credit limit, minimum payment.
MX_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.masking: Mapped to an amount between 1,000 and 5,000,000.

MX_FIN_INGRESO_MENSUAL.title: Monthly income
MX_FIN_INGRESO_MENSUAL.what: Salary, perceptions, net pay, household income.
MX_FIN_INGRESO_MENSUAL.masking: Mapped to an amount between 8,000 and 250,000.

MX_FIN_AFORE.masking: Replaced by one of the ten AFOREs authorized by CONSAR in 2026.

MX_FIN_SALDO_RETIRO.what: Balances of the retirement and housing subaccounts, voluntary savings, pension amounts.

MX_FIN_CREDITO_VIVIENDA.what: Infonavit, Fovissste, Cofinavit or bank mortgage, and payroll discount notices.

MX_FIN_SEGURIDAD_SOCIAL.what: Derechohabiencia: IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar, Pemex, armed forces, private insurance, none. It reveals formal or informal work.

closing.title: Check digits computed by the set
body: Mexican applications validate their keys, and a masked key that fails validation breaks the test it was meant for. Two keys are covered by the plugin's own frameworks: the CLABE by Check Digit (weights 3, 7, 1, modulo 10), and the NSS by Payment Card, since its check digit is Luhn — the check of payment cards. The CURP and the RFC need more:

list: **CURP** — every character counts, letters included (`0`–`9`, `A`–`N` → 10–23, `Ñ` 24, `O`–`Z` → 25–36), with weights 18 down to 2, modulo 10. Check Digit reads letters in base 36, where `O`–`Z` are worth one less.

**RFC** — the SAT table (`&` 24, space 37, `Ñ` 38), weights 13 down to 2, modulo 11, with 10 written `A`. A company RFC counts as if preceded by a space. Check Digit writes a result of 10 as `0` and does not accept `&` or `Ñ`.

body: For these two the set computes the check digit itself. After the body is masked, a running sum travels through the value two characters at a time: a lookup table turns *sum + next two characters* into *those characters + new sum*, and the last table writes the check digit in place. Each table lists only what its positions can hold — digits for the date, letters for the names — so the CURP takes 8 steps and the RFC 6, each a Regex Decompose and a Data Cleansing file generated with the set, in a single String Algorithm Chain.

Every masked CURP, RFC and NSS is valid, and the mapping stays one-to-one — a key cannot collide with another. The cost is paid per value, per step, not per algorithm configured. Measured with the plugin outside the engine, on a laptop, a CURP masks in about 11 µs, an RFC in about 9 and an NSS in about 3, against about 2 for a Character Mapping: some 90,000 CURPs per second per thread. Half of the CURP's cost is its body — the date, and the keyed lookups for sex and state; the check digit is the other half. An engine's throughput depends on its hardware and job settings.

closing.title: Dates inside keys
body: CURP, RFC and the INE voter key carry the birth date as `YYMMDD`. Leaving it would leave the strongest quasi-identifier in the key; changing its digits freely would produce dates that do not exist.

The decade stays and the unit of the year is masked, as in a birth year column. The month goes through a one-to-one mapping of 1–12, the day through one of 1–28, 29–30 among themselves, and a 31st keeps a 31-day month. The result is always a real date, and two different dates never become the same.

The same algorithm masks the date in the three keys, so a person's CURP, RFC and voter key keep agreeing with each other. They do not agree with the birth date column, which moves by up to 60 days: no algorithm can see two columns at once.

list: **Binary columns** — photos of INE credentials, fingerprint images, clinical PDFs stored in BLOBs — cannot be masked by these algorithms. Inventory them and report them as residual risk.

**Keys and the columns they derive from.** The letters of a masked CURP or RFC no longer come from the masked name, and its date is not the masked birth date. Where an application recomputes the CURP from the name, it will not match.
**Inconvenient words.** RENAPO replaces some offensive letter combinations at the start of a CURP; a masked CURP may form one. It still passes the check digit.
**Lowercase or formatted keys** — a CURP in lower case, an NSS with dashes — are masked character by character, without a valid check digit.

**Municipalities** spelled in a way the list does not know pass unchanged. A name shared by a large and a small municipality stays as it is; the 5-digit code has no such ambiguity. A 3-digit municipality code without its state is not generalized.

**Free text** is redacted word by word: a phone number written with spaces (`55 1234 5678`) is not found there, and a given name that is also a common word (`Luz`, `Paz`, `Rosa`) is redacted wherever it appears.
**Minors** — a birth date moves at most 60 days, so few people cross their 18th birthday, but some do. Where that matters, split the rule by age group with Multi-Column Condition.
**Addresses** are replaced as a whole line. Street, colonia, postal code and municipality in separate columns are masked independently and no longer form a coherent address.
**Plates and VINs** keep their format but not the state series or the VIN check digit.

closing.title: Verification
body: The set is generated and checked by two scripts kept with it in the repository:

list: `build.mjs` generates the set, its lookup tables and its check digit tables from its definitions and hand-kept lists.

`verify.mjs` reviews every classifier configuration, profiles 151 columns with the whole set at its threshold — well named, badly named, and 26 columns that are not personal data — and masks 350 sample values and 228 placeholders such as `S/D` through the running app. Random CURPs, RFCs, NSS and CLABEs are checked for a valid check digit and a valid date, 150 of each for collisions, and pairs of CURP and RFC of the same person for agreement.

body: At the last build every column was assigned as expected and every value masked as expected.

list: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares — DOF 20 March 2025, last amendment DOF 14 November 2025 (Cámara de Diputados). The 2010 law, DOF 5 July 2010, for comparison.
CURP structure and check digit — Registro Nacional de Población (RENAPO).
RFC check digit — Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT). Tax regime catalog `c_RegimenFiscal` — SAT, CFDI 4.0.
NSS structure — Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS). CLABE — Banco de México and the Asociación de Bancos de México.
INE voter key — Instituto Nacional Electoral. National political parties, including the registration of Partido Paz and Somos México on 1 July 2026 — INE.
Municipalities, geostatistical codes, coordinates and population — INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020. Religion, disability, schooling and housing categories — the same census.
Most frequent surnames — INE and RENAPO registers. Given names — INEGI and name frequency registers.
Indigenous peoples — Instituto Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas, Catálogo Nacional de Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas y Afromexicanas (2024).
AFOREs — Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (CONSAR), 2026. Social programs — Programas para el Bienestar, Government of Mexico, 2026.
Socioeconomic levels — Asociación Mexicana de Agencias de Inteligencia de Mercado y Opinión (AMAI).
Ten-digit dialing — Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones, 3 August 2019. Postal codes — Correos de México (SEPOMEX). License plates — NOM-001-SCT-2-2016.
